assessment.nobel_worthiness: A prediction that was tested by nature almost at once: kilonova emission from a neutron-star merger was calculated before GW170817 and then seen in the optical and infrared afterglow. It gives direct evidence that r-process heavy elements such as gold are made in mergers, which has the existential flavour of telling us where we come from, and it is a flagship result of multi-messenger astronomy. Here the discovery clearly leads and the people follow.
assessment.attribution: The theory side is reasonably clear (Metzger and collaborators for the kilonova/macronova model and its heating, Kasen for radiative-transfer opacities and light curves). Tanvir represents the observational side, from the short-GRB afterglow excess and the GW170817 counterpart campaigns. The observational credit is shared with very large collaborations and with other groups (e.g. Li and Paczynski for the original macronova idea), so a three-person split is defensible but not obviously the only fair one.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by GW170817/AT2017gfo with many independent follow-up teams and by later candidate events. The interpretation (lanthanide opacity, ejecta composition) is still refined, but the core discovery is stable. Timing looks good, since the gravitational-wave detection itself was recognised in 2017.
uncertainties: The share between the early macronova proposers, the detailed modelling groups and the observers is contested and I cannot verify it from memory.
The extent to which kilonovae are the dominant r-process site is still debated.
Whether the committee sees this as a distinct discovery or as a follow-on to the 2017 prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery of a diffuse flux of astrophysical neutrinos at TeV to PeV energies, and later the first source associations (the blazar TXS 0506+056 and the Galactic plane), opens neutrino astronomy and uses a cubic kilometre of Antarctic ice as the detector. It is a clear experimental discovery of the kind I want, a new window on the universe that arrived with clues from nature rather than from theory.
assessment.attribution: Halzen is the intellectual driver of the IceCube concept and its predecessors (AMANDA), but this is a collaboration of hundreds, and the supplied credit lists only one name. A single-laureate prize would be unusual for a discovery of this scale. Other founding figures in neutrino telescopes (e.g. the DUMAND and Baikal pioneers) and key IceCube leaders could plausibly be included, though I may only select from the supplied string.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux was established in 2013 and has since been confirmed with several channels. The source associations are newer, at roughly the 3 to 4 sigma level for individual objects, with KM3NeT and Baikal-GVD now adding independent data. Recognition is reasonably timely, though the field is still maturing.
uncertainties: The supplied credit is a single person, which may not reflect fair allocation for a large collaboration.
Individual source identifications remain statistically modest.
The origin of the bulk of the diffuse flux is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and the Z2 topological insulator, followed by the observation in HgTe quantum wells and in 3D materials, brought a new organising principle of matter. It has been tested extensively in many materials and has shaped condensed-matter research for two decades. It is a theory prediction that nature confirmed, which is the pattern I trust most.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the decisive theoretical step. Molenkamp's group delivered the first experimental realisation, after the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal. That means Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang, along with Fu and Moore for the 3D case, are also plausible but are not in this credited set. Kane, Mele and Molenkamp is a coherent trio from the supplied names, though the omission is a real fairness question.
assessment.maturity: Very mature. Independent experiments (HgTe, Bi-Sb, Bi2Se3 by ARPES) have confirmed the picture for over fifteen years. Practical impact is still limited, but the concept is firmly established, so recognition is not premature.
uncertainties: Omitted contributors (Bernevig, Zhang, Fu, Moore, Hasan) could weaken the claim that this trio is complete.
The quantum spin Hall effect in HgTe has quantisation imperfections at longer lengths.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: A prediction of flat bands at the magic angle in twisted bilayer graphene, followed by the observation of correlated insulators and superconductivity in 2018, created the field of moire quantum materials. It combines a clean theoretical idea with a striking experimental demonstration, and it has given a tunable platform for strongly correlated physics.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the 2011 prediction, and Jarillo-Herrero's group made the 2018 experimental discovery with Cao and others. A trio of two theorists and one experimentalist is a natural configuration, though the early experimental graduate students and other groups (e.g. Dean, Young, Yacoby, Mak and Shan) also contributed to the broader field.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced by many groups, and the field has developed quickly. The mechanism of superconductivity is still unsettled, and the discovery is less than a decade old, so some committee members may find it a bit early. Nevertheless the confirmation of the central claims is broad.
uncertainties: The pairing mechanism of the superconductivity is not agreed.
Sample inhomogeneity and twist-angle disorder complicate the interpretation of some observations.
Whether it is early compared with the typical Nobel lag.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Inflation solves the horizon and flatness puzzles and, through the quantum fluctuations Mukhanov and collaborators computed, explains the seeds of cosmic structure. The predicted nearly scale-invariant adiabatic spectrum has been confirmed in great detail by COBE, WMAP and Planck. As a cosmologist I find this important, but as someone who insists on clues from nature I note that the inflationary paradigm itself is not yet distinguished from alternatives.
assessment.attribution: Guth for the original proposal, Linde for new and chaotic inflation, and Mukhanov for the quantum origin of perturbations is a sensible set from the supplied names. Starobinsky, Albrecht, Steinhardt, Sato, Chibisov and others have strong claims, so the credit is contested and the three-person limit is painful here.
assessment.maturity: The perturbation spectrum is confirmed, but there is no detection of primordial gravitational waves, and the nature of the inflaton is unknown. I regard the discovery as important but not conclusively established, so this is arguably premature, and I give it a moderate rank.
uncertainties: No detection of primordial B-modes, so the inflationary mechanism remains unproven.
Priority disputes (Starobinsky, Sato and others) and the three-laureate cap.
Concerns about eternal inflation and the multiverse.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The measurement of a surprisingly large theta-13 by Daya Bay and RENO (with Double Chooz and T2K contributing) opened the way to CP-violation searches in the lepton sector. It is a clean experimental discovery with a precise result and a clear connection to the 2015 prize on neutrino oscillations.
assessment.attribution: Daya Bay (Wang as spokesperson, Luk as co-spokesperson) and RENO (Kim) announced the result within weeks of each other in 2012. Double Chooz and T2K played a role in the early indications, and the collaborations are large. The supplied trio is a reasonable but debatable choice because the contributions of the Double Chooz and T2K teams may be left out.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed with improving precision since 2012, and it is now a standard input to global fits. Timing is fine, although the committee has already honoured neutrino oscillations, which may make this a follow-on rather than a stand-alone discovery.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2015 prize may reduce its standing as a separate discovery.
Credit relative to Double Chooz and T2K is open.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices implement Hubbard-type models in a controlled setting, with the Mott transition, quantum gas microscopy and tunable interactions. The idea (Jaksch, Zoller and collaborators) was followed by experiments, and the results give a real laboratory for many-body questions. It is a decisive example of theory and experiment working together.
assessment.attribution: Zoller and Cirac for the theoretical proposals, and Bloch (Mott insulator experiments, microscopy) for the experiments, would form a natural trio. Greiner and Dalibard are also strong, and Jaksch is not in the supplied list. This candidate overlaps heavily with B001, B042 and B044, so the committee would need to pick one coherent framing of the cold-atom and quantum-information area.
assessment.maturity: Mature and independently confirmed across many labs. It is an active and fruitful field, although the 2001 and 2012 prizes already recognised neighbouring cold-atom and quantum-control work.
uncertainties: Overlap with other quantum-simulation candidates, and the question of which proposal to reward.
Whether quantum simulators have yet answered an open physical question that existing methods could not.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, built on the magic-wavelength idea, has taken timekeeping to the 10^-18 level, which tests fundamental constants and general relativity in the laboratory, and enables relativistic geodesy. It is a measurement discovery with a clear, concrete and checkable outcome, which I value.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice clock, and Ye's group achieved its best performance and many of the practical demonstrations. The two-person configuration is clean. Other clock pioneers (Hall and Hansch were honoured in 2005; Wineland in 2012) are already recognised, so the overlap is not damaging.
assessment.maturity: The performance is confirmed by several independent labs and is now moving towards a redefinition of the second. This is a mature, timely result, but its fundamental-physics payoff (e.g. dark matter or constant-drift limits) is still mainly null, so its significance rests on metrology.
uncertainties: It may be seen as an incremental advance on earlier prizes in frequency metrology.
Fundamental-physics payoffs have so far been constraints rather than discoveries.
